name: Kitchen/countertop cleaners
governing_basis: No sovereign sets heavy-metal maximums for hard-surface / incidental-dermal cleaning products; the eco-label and disclosure regimes (EPA Safer Choice, Green Seal GS-8, CA SB 258, NY Household Cleaner Disclosure Act) are ingredient-disclosure and eco-labeling regimes, not heavy-metal MLs. The toxic panel (Pb/tAs/Cd/tHg) is read across from the nearest applicable coherent sovereign regime (China NMPA 2015 mandatory cosmetic trace-metal limits), conservative because a cosmetic is prolonged leave-on skin contact and a hard-surface cleaner is incidental dermal. Basis: total content in the product as placed on the market.
native_basis_label: total heavy-metal content in product as placed on the market (mg/kg product)
scope_note: Cleaners for kitchen and food-preparation surfaces. Food-preparation surfaces create a food-residue-transfer (ingestion) sub-pathway; GB 14930.1 Type B (food-contact-equipment cleaning) is a relevant conservative reference for that sub-pathway, but the binding basis is total content in the product as placed on the market with a cosmetics/personal-care read-across for the primary incidental-dermal pathway.

Pb.basis: total lead content, product as placed on the market (mg/kg)
Pb.label: Read across from China NMPA 2015 mandatory cosmetic lead limit (10 mg/kg), a coherent statutory finished-consumer-chemical-product ceiling, conservative for an incidental-dermal cleaning product. No cleaning-product-specific lead ML exists in any jurisdiction.

tAs.basis: total arsenic content, product as placed on the market (mg/kg)
tAs.label: Read across from China NMPA 2015 mandatory cosmetic total-arsenic limit (2 mg/kg). No cleaning-product-specific arsenic ML exists for hard-surface products (GB 14930.1 covers only food/tableware-cleaning detergents).

iAs.rationale: No jurisdiction sets an inorganic-arsenic limit for cleaning products; the consumer-chemical trace-metal instruments regulate TOTAL arsenic (see the tAs cell), which bounds the inorganic fraction (iAs <= tAs). No routed occurrence source measured or speciated inorganic arsenic in these products.
iAs.regulatory_basis: Bounded by the total-arsenic read-across ceiling (NMPA 2015, 2 mg/kg); no inorganic-arsenic limit for cleaning products in any jurisdiction
iAs.jurisdictions_checked: CN GB 14930.1; CN NMPA 2015; EU 10/2011; EU REACH Annex XVII; US EPA Safer Choice; Green Seal GS-8; CA SB 258; NY Household Cleaner Disclosure; Health Canada; Germany BfR
iAs.cross_sourced: parent tAs published (NMPA read-across) + credible-ML register checked 2026-08-13 (no iAs cleaning-product limit); occurrence corpus measured no arsenic speciation
iAs.reference_method: Total-arsenic screen by ICP-MS; reflex inorganic-arsenic speciation only if total arsenic approaches the read-across ceiling.

Cd.basis: total cadmium content, product as placed on the market (mg/kg)
Cd.label: Read across from China NMPA 2015 mandatory cosmetic cadmium limit (5 mg/kg). No cleaning-product-specific cadmium ML exists in any jurisdiction.

tHg.basis: total mercury content, product as placed on the market (mg/kg)
tHg.label: Read across from China NMPA 2015 mandatory cosmetic mercury limit (1 mg/kg). No cleaning-product-specific mercury ML exists in any jurisdiction.

MeHg.rationale: Methylmercury has no formation or migration pathway in a cleaning formulation; it is a marine-bioaccumulation speciation. The consumer-chemical mercury instruments regulate total mercury (see the tHg cell), which bounds any organomercury fraction. No routed occurrence source measured or speciated methylmercury in these products.
MeHg.regulatory_basis: Bounded by the total-mercury read-across ceiling (NMPA 2015, 1 mg/kg); no methylmercury limit for cleaning products in any jurisdiction
MeHg.jurisdictions_checked: CN GB 14930.1; CN NMPA 2015; EU 10/2011; EU REACH Annex XVII; US EPA Safer Choice; Green Seal GS-8; CA SB 258; NY Household Cleaner Disclosure; Health Canada; Germany BfR
MeHg.cross_sourced: parent tHg published (NMPA read-across) + credible-ML register checked 2026-08-13 (no MeHg cleaning-product limit); occurrence corpus screened, no organomercury speciation reported
MeHg.reference_method: Total-mercury screen by CV-AAS or ICP-MS; no reflex methylmercury speciation defined for cleaning products (no formation pathway).

Ni.reference_method: Total nickel by ICP-MS on the product as placed on market (acid digestion).
Ni.escalation_rule: Nickel is a confirmed dermal sensitizer and is measured in household cleaning products (zhang2010; ecetoc1992). No jurisdiction sets a numeric total-nickel maximum for cleaning products, so certification screens total nickel and escalates a lot above the running category control band to ALARA review rather than pass/failing on an invented number.
Ni.rationale: Present in the occurrence corpus; no sovereign ML in a consumer-chemical total-content basis. Article-migration/drinking-water nickel values are a different basis and are not read across.

Al.reference_method: Total aluminium by ICP-MS on the product as placed on market.
Al.escalation_rule: Aluminium is Tier-2 and may be a functional mineral ingredient (alumina abrasives in scouring cleaners, aluminosilicate builders). No jurisdiction sets a cleaning-product aluminium maximum. Screen total aluminium; a lot outside the functional-ingredient expectation triggers ingredient review.
Al.rationale: No sovereign ML; potential functional-ingredient source means a not-material claim would be false. Screen, do not publish a number.

Cr-total.reference_method: Total chromium by ICP-MS on the product as placed on market.
Cr-total.escalation_rule: Total chromium is measured in cleaning products (zhang2010; ecetoc1992). No jurisdiction sets a cleaning-product chromium maximum. Screen total chromium and reflex Cr(VI) speciation where total chromium is elevated or the formulation is oxidizing/acidic.
Cr-total.rationale: Present in the occurrence corpus; no sovereign ML in a consumer-chemical total-content basis.

Cr-VI.reference_method: Hexavalent chromium by IC-ICP-MS with alkaline extraction (US EPA 3060A / 7199) on oxidizing or acidic formulations.
Cr-VI.escalation_rule: Cr(VI) is measured in some consumer cleaning products (ecetoc1992) and oxidizing/acidic chemistries (bleach, oven, toilet, descaler) can stabilize it. No jurisdiction sets a cleaning-product Cr(VI) maximum. Reflex Cr(VI) speciation on oxidizing/acidic formulations and where total chromium is elevated; escalate a positive Cr(VI) result to ALARA review.
Cr-VI.rationale: Measured in the corpus; a real hazard on oxidizing chemistries; no sovereign number, so a method + escalation rule is published rather than an invented threshold.

Sn.rationale: Inorganic tin has no source in a hard-surface cleaning formulation (no tinplate/canned-food pathway). Organotin is a DISTINCT species (biocide/stabiliser) restricted by REACH Annex XVII entry 20 and screened separately where a formulation could carry it; it does not bound, and is not bounded by, this inorganic-tin cell. No jurisdiction sets an inorganic-tin limit for cleaning products, and no routed occurrence source measured tin.
Sn.regulatory_basis: No inorganic-tin limit for cleaning products in any jurisdiction; organotin covered separately under REACH Annex XVII entry 20
Sn.jurisdictions_checked: CN GB 14930.1; CN NMPA 2015; EU 10/2011; EU REACH Annex XVII (entry 20 organotin); US EPA Safer Choice; Green Seal GS-8; CA SB 258; NY Household Cleaner Disclosure; Health Canada
Sn.cross_sourced: credible-ML register checked 2026-08-13 (no inorganic-Sn cleaning-product limit; only organotin restriction, a distinct species); occurrence corpus measured no tin
Sn.reference_method: Periodic ICP-MS inorganic-tin verification; organotin (DBT/DOT/TBT as Sn) screened separately by GC-ICP-MS where a biocidal-organotin pathway is plausible.

method: HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit default, consumer-chemical form; native basis = total heavy-metal content in product as placed on market, mg/kg; no cross-basis min)
